A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dextrose is the best source of carbohydrate for young chicks, followed in decreasing order of preference by corn flour, waxy corn and rice flour.
dextrose is the preferred carbohydrate source in chick diets, and it is more efficient than corn, corn flour or rice flour, especially at younger ages.
chicks fed the dextrinized-cornstarch diet had the highest growth performance, and the high-amylose-starch and pregelatinize-unmodified-cornstarch diets had lowest growth performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carbohydrate sources that we tested had a significant impact on the ME of diets for chicks.
MEn values of diets fed to chicks can be significantly affected by the carbohydrate source, and the MEn values increase with age for most diets.
the chick’s ability to utilize carbohydrates is affected by the source of the carbohydrate and by the age of the bird, with younger birds being less able to utilize carbohydrates.
